foundation.work: Listen for: the tens digit going up by one. If the answer is 65, the child may have added 1 to the whole number: ask them to point to the tens digit.

foundation.q: Put these numbers in order, smallest first: 58, 85, 49.
foundation.work: Listen for: looking at the tens digit first. Any way of working is fine. If the order starts with 85, the child may have read "smallest" as "biggest": ask them to read the question aloud.
Listen for a strategy: take away 6 then 3, count on from 9, or use fingers. Every method is welcome.
Listen for: adding the tens to the tens. If the answer is 48 or 345, ask the child to say what 30 is made of.

core.q: A pattern goes triangle, circle, circle, square, triangle, circle, circle, square, and keeps going. What is the 10th shape?
core.work: Listen for: finding the group of 4. Drawing out all 10 shapes or counting on in 4s both work. If the answer is square, the child may have found the 8th shape: ask them to count on two more.

core.q: 5? + 27 = 81. The ? hides one digit. Which digit is it?
core.work: Listen for: taking 27 away from 81 (54), or trying a digit and checking it. Both are fine. If the answer is 5 or 6, ask the child to check by adding.

core.q: A stack of cubes has 2 layers. Each layer has 3 rows with 4 cubes in each row. How many cubes are in the stack?
core.work: Listen for: finding one layer first (12), then doubling. Drawing, skip counting and repeated adding are all fine. If the answer is 9, the child may have added 2 + 3 + 4: ask them to draw one layer.

core.q: A film starts at 3:50 p.m. and lasts 25 minutes. What time does it end?
core.work: Listen for: counting on to 4:00 first (10 minutes), then 15 more. Accept 4:15 with or without p.m. If the answer is 3:75, the child may have added 25 to the minutes: ask how many minutes are in an hour.

core.q: A pen costs $1.20. A ruler costs $0.85. How much do they cost together?
core.work: Listen for: dollars and cents added with care (120 cents + 85 cents = 205 cents) or counting on with coins. Accept $2.05 or 2.05. If the answer is $1.105 or $2.5, ask the child to show it with coins.

core.q: A pizza is cut into 4 equal parts. I eat 3 parts. What fraction of the pizza did I eat?
core.work: Listen for: the bottom number tells how many equal parts. If the answer is 1/4, the child may have named the part that is left: ask how many parts were eaten.

stretch.q: These last two are tricky on purpose, so it is fine to skip them. I think of a number. I double it, then add 3, and I get 17. What was my number?
stretch.work: Listen for: working backwards (17 - 3 = 14, half of 14) or guess and check. Both are fine.

stretch.q: Ali, Mei, Siti and Ben each have a different pet: cat, dog, fish or rabbit. Siti has the rabbit. Ben does not have the cat or the fish. Mei does not have the cat. Who has the cat?
stretch.work: Listen for: crossing out as they go (Siti rabbit, then Ben dog, then Mei fish, so Ali has the cat). Any way of working is fine.

childNote: These two are tricky on purpose. Have a go, and it is fine to skip them.

scoring.warmupRule: If the warm-up score is 2 or less, one level down may be the more comfortable start.
scoring.stretchIsAFlag: Brain stretchers are not part of the placement score. If a child solves one or both, tell your tutor: they may enjoy the Go further pages. Level-up check only when main 6 of 6, warm-up 4 of 4 and both brain stretchers.
scoring.scoreLine: Warm-up: ____ / 4     Main questions: ____ / 6     Brain stretchers (a bonus, not scored for placement): ____ / 2

parent.join: Join Ages 7-9 (Level 2). Your child has the foundations and will be well challenged. If they scored 6 of 6 on the main questions and 4 of 4 on the warm-up, and solved both brain stretchers, you can also try the Ages 8-10 (Level 3) check.
parent.support: Join Ages 7-9 (Level 2). Most children here find some of the puzzles tricky; that is what the class is for. Your tutor will check in with you after Lesson 1. If the warm-up score is 2 or less, Ages 6-8 (Level 1) may be a more comfortable start - talk to us first.
parent.down: We suggest a chat with your tutor and a free taster before choosing. Ages 6-8 (Level 1) builds the same thinking habits with smaller numbers. If your child is 9 or older, ask us: you do not have to choose a level by age.
parent.strongBox:
Strong?
Choose the level that fits the score, not the school year. A child who finds this easy will enjoy the Go further pages in class.
parent.gentleBox:
Want a gentler start?
Starting one level down means more wins early on and more joy in class.

tutorKey.header: Print pages 1 and 2 for your child. Keep pages 3 and 4 for yourself.
tutorKey.tieBreak: Borderline (4 of the 6 main marks): ask your child to explain main questions 6, 8 and 9 aloud. If they can say why, use the higher band. If a child finishes in under 12 minutes, ask them to check two answers before you mark.
tutorKey.prereq: Main questions 7, 8, 9 and 10 (cube stacks and arrays, time, money, fractions) are topics taught in school. Missing two or more means Lessons 3, 6, 7, 8 and 9 will need extra care, even if the main score is 5 or 6.
